sonnet.problem: The question says 'the righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon someone.' The right answer, 'The righteous man himself,' repeats the same words, so the question holds a form of its own answer.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The blank sits in a near-verbatim line of the verse ('Repent and ___ from all your transgressions'). The baker is filling in the wording of the line, not reasoning out a meaning. 'Turn' is also the word the earlier cards in this stop already used repeatedly.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. ... The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The card asks what 'a new heart and a new spirit' means and makes 'A change on the inside' the right answer. Verse 31 never says what the picture stands for. The question also already contains 'heart' and 'spirit,' which hand over the answer.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. ... This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.
